trust_decision.summary: The ESM compiler decides whether identifier text taken from a module's import/export clauses may be spliced into the generated wrapper source evaluated by VM.Script; for import-brace names/aliases it only strips quotes before interpolation.

landing_point.why: Advisory names 'import alias'; the import-braces branch is the only place aliases are split and interpolated into `let {...} = $happy_dom.imports.get(...)`.

fix_sites.entry_point: ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.compile() via ECMAScriptModule.evaluate()/preload() (packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModule.ts:188-190), i.e. <script type=module> / modulepreload / dynamic import when enableJavaScriptEvaluation is on
same: import { name as alias } / import { name } clause parsing in compile()
same: generated `let {...}` destructuring; sanitised values also flow into the circular-import resolver at packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.ts:477

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report says 'import alias'; export-from and export-object names are a different statement kind, export-object was already 'fixed' by the earlier GHSA-6q6h-j7hj-3r64 (VALID_VARIABLE_NAME_REGEXP at line 385, test at test/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.test.ts:776), and their names land inside quoted string literals, so a solver can argue they are inert data, not code.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unicode / $-containing local bindings (e.g. `import { valid as ünicode$1 }`) and quoted module-namespace names must keep compiling; reusing the ASCII-only VALID_VARIABLE_NAME_REGEXP, or rejecting quoted names, breaks them (the fix test asserts `let {"valid": ünicode$1}`).

O6_input_shapes: aliased form `name as <alias-with-extra-tokens>` (alias validated against Unicode identifier regex)
un-aliased form `<name-with-extra-tokens>` (alias defaults to name, same validation)
imported name containing quotes, backslash, CR/LF, U+2028/U+2029 (stripped, then emitted via JSON.stringify)
legitimate Unicode identifier alias must still pass

O8_uncovered_routes.route: export { a as b } from 'url' (re-export): both export and import names are spliced into single-quoted literals with only quotes stripped; a backslash is not removed and can terminate the literal.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Re-export is 'export', not 'import alias'; names sit inside string literals so look like data.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~50 lines below landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: export { local as name }: importName is regex-validated (prior GHSA) but exportName is only quote-stripped before going into a single-quoted literal.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Already hardened by the previous advisory (line 385), so a solver assumes it is done.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: export var/let/const declared names (plain list and destructuring) are emitted raw both as a string key and as an expression in newCodeEnd.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The original declaration text is also emitted verbatim, so the names must already be valid JS for the module to compile; looks like no extra exposure.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Widen the `export * as name` capture (STATEMENT_REGEXP group 9, line 33) to accept quoted string names, then splice it quote-stripped into `$happy_dom.exports['...']`.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ES2022 allows arbitrary string export names (`export * as "a b" from`); a maintainer adding that support would naturally reuse the quote-strip idiom used everywhere else in the file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Module cache keyed by moduleURL replays previously compiled code; a variant that caches per-import binding lists and re-renders them later (circular-resolver style, line 477) would bypass a check placed only at compile-time parsing.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Cache already exists for performance; storing parsed bindings instead of full code is a plausible optimisation, giving a how-type producer the check never calls.

O9_family: CWE-94 code injection via string-built code generation (identifier text spliced into generated JS)

out_of_scope_notes: SECURITY.md:16-18 states the VM context is not a security sandbox and JS evaluation is off by default; the marginal impact of identifier injection over already-executing module code is debatable.
ElementEventAttributeUtility.ts:45-70 wraps attribute text in a function for evaluateScript, but that text is the handler code itself, not a sibling.
